Invariant review of fix/poll-intervals: the "cannot drift silently" claim is false today, and the two new tests guard one literal each, not the sync. Four findings, file:line, with one structural fix that closes all of them.

FINDING 1 — CRITICAL. The claim is already falsified inside the same package the "source of truth" lives in.
Claim: internal/mcp/poll_tools_test.go:250-251 and :261-262 ("keeping ... in sync with internal/email/config.go's validPollIntervals rather than drifting silently"; "cannot drift silently").
Falsifying case, present on the branch right now: validPollIntervals (internal/email/config.go:182-192) gained 2m and 3m, and two enumerations in internal/email/poller.go were NOT updated:
  - poller.go:104  `"invalid poll_interval %q in config (valid: 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, n=disable)"` — reachable: Poller.Start() on a hand-edited email.json with e.g. "4m" prints a valid-set that omits 2m and 3m.
  - poller.go:316  InvalidIntervalError.Error(): `"must be 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, or n"` — today only reachable by a direct Poller.SetInterval caller (the MCP handler pre-checks ValidPollInterval at poll_tools.go:124 so its own message at :126 fires first), but the text is wrong and becomes user-facing the moment anything else calls SetInterval.
  Also DESIGN.md:504 still lists the old set.
This is exactly the drift the tests say cannot happen, and no test caught it. (TestPoller_SetInterval_Invalid at poller_test.go:56-62 only checks the error type, not its text.)

FINDING 2 — HIGH. TestSetPollInterval_3mSucceeds (poll_tools_test.go:253-259) does not test sync; there is nothing in poll_tools.go to be in sync. Acceptance is fully delegated to email.ValidPollInterval at poll_tools.go:124 — the handler has no accepted set of its own. The only things in poll_tools.go that can drift are three prose strings (:34, :38, :126). Trace: add "4m" to validPollIntervals and forget poll_tools.go entirely → test passes (3m is still accepted). Remove "3m" from validPollIntervals → test fails, but only because 3m is the one hardcoded fixture. It proves "3m is accepted today", nothing more.

FINDING 3 — HIGH. TestSetPollInterval_InvalidErrorListsFullSet (poll_tools_test.go:264-273) asserts Contains "2m" and Contains "3m" against the whole result text. Trace: add "4m" (or anything) to validPollIntervals, forget line 126 → passes; the test cannot see a NEW value. Remove "2m" from the :126 string → fails, so that one direction is caught, but only for the two literals the author typed. Secondary fragility: the result text starts with `invalid interval %q` echoing the INPUT, so Contains("2m") is satisfiable by the fixture alone — change the fixture to "12m" or "2min" and the assertion passes with 2m deleted from the valid list. Current fixture "4m" happens not to collide.

FINDING 4 — HIGH. Zero assertions cover the tool description strings at poll_tools.go:34 and :38, and nothing guards plugin/commands/inbox.md.
  - The only description-reading helper, pollStatusDesc (poll_tools_test.go:83-103), reads get_poll_status only. No test reads set_poll_interval's description or its input-schema description from tools/list. Confirmed by grep: no test in internal/mcp references "Valid intervals" or "Polling interval:".
  - inbox.md: no Go test, no script, no Makefile target reads it; only markdownlint touches it. It holds TWO hand-maintained copies per value: the enumeration (argument-hint line 3, lines 20 and 26) and the interval→cron mapping (lines 44-46). A new interval added to config.go lands silently with the /inbox skill unable to parse it and no cron expression for it.

Tally of hand-maintained copies of the set outside config.go: poll_tools.go ×3 (:34, :38, :126), poller.go ×2 (:104, :316), inbox.md ×3 (hint, prose, cron table), README.md ×2 (:140, :150), DESIGN.md ×1. Nine copies, two already stale on this branch.

Silent-failure pass on release-daemon: zero findings. Every failure path in the diff stops the pipeline loudly. Each claim below was verified by running the construct, not by reading it.

1. Workflow for-loop, .github/workflows/release.yml:26-31. GitHub Actions runs `run:` blocks with `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`. Under those flags a failing `go build` inside the loop body aborts the whole step: I reproduced with a loop whose body is `echo; false; echo` and the second echo never printed, exit 1. So a daemon build failing for one os/arch fails the "Build binaries" step and no later step runs. No partial set reaches the release step.

2. Checksums, .github/workflows/release.yml:35. `sha256sum beadle-email-* beadle-daemon-*` fails loudly on an unmatched glob. With no files: both globs are passed literally, sha256sum prints `'beadle-daemon-*': No such file or directory` and exits 1. With only email binaries present it still exits 1 and prints the error for the daemon glob, even though it writes the email lines to checksums.txt. Since the step exits non-zero, the release step is never reached.

3. Makefile dist target, Makefile:177-188. Each recipe line is a separate shell invocation and make stops the recipe at the first line that exits non-zero (no `-` prefix, no `.IGNORE`, no `.ONESHELL`; `make -n dist` confirms the eight build lines and the checksum line are plain lines).
